This issue might be a duplicate of an existing issue. Please check:
- #20640: Same `{env:VAR}` substitution breaking on Windows with backslash paths causing `InvalidEscapeCharacter`. That issue was closed with a different proposed fix (forward-slash replacement), but the symptom and affected code path are the same.

If your issue is distinct from #20640 (e.g., you believe the correct fix is `JSON.stringify()`-based escaping rather than the slash-replacement workaround), please clarify the difference in this issue so maintainers can evaluate it separately.

#20640 was closed by the author as "incorrect root cause attribution" (it cited a non-existent file `paths.ts`). The corrected issue was never filed, so the bug still exists.

This report differs in two ways:

1. Correct file path: the actual code is in `packages/opencode/src/config/variable.ts`, not `paths.ts`.

2. Correct fix: #20640 proposed `replaceAll("\", "/")` as a fix, but that is a workaround that only papers over the real problem. The right fix is to make `{env:}` consistent with `{file:}` — the latter already wraps with `JSON.stringify()` to escape backslashes properly. The `{env:}` path should do the same.

```ts
// variable.ts - current (broken)
text.replace(/\{env:([^}]+)\}/g, (_, v) => process.env[v] || '')

// should be (like {file:} already does)
text.replace(/\{env:([^}]+)\}/g, (_, v) => JSON.stringify(process.env[v] || '').slice(1, -1))
```

The slash-replacement approach would also break cases where a literal backslash is intentional in a non-path context.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #30249: MCP tool results with non-image binary content being mishandled — same root cause (non-image/non-PDF blob MIME types not supported), though that issue manifests as a crash while this one is a silent omission.

This may be related to, or the same root cause as, #30249.

What seems common between the two reports:
- both involve MCP tool results that return a `resource` / `EmbeddedResource` with a populated base64 `blob`
- both involve non-image resources
- both appear to fail in OpenCode's handling of the returned resource, rather than in the MCP server itself

What is different in this report:
- the MIME type is `text/markdown`
- the server is [`mcp-atlassian`](https://github.com/sooperset/mcp-atlassian)
- in this case OpenCode does not crash the session, but omits the resource from model-visible context and renders it as:

```text
[Binary MCP resource omitted: attachment:///EXAMPLE-123/example-implementation-plan.md (text/markdown, 30 KB) is not a supported attachment type]
```

I verified with MCP Inspector that the raw tool result contains a valid `EmbeddedResource` with:
- `mimeType: "text/markdown"`
- a populated `blob`
- a normal `attachment:///...` URI

So even if this ends up being closed as a duplicate of #30249, this issue adds a concrete `text/markdown` reproduction and shows that the bug also affects textual MCP resources that should likely be readable by the model rather than treated as unsupported binary attachments.

Root-cause update (2026-07-06, sanitized):

- Confirmed recurrence in production. A paid orphan subscription remains active in Stripe, but because it is not linked to workspace billing it grants no workspace entitlement.
- At [`origin/dev` `38bb38e`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/38bb38ecb2b50f81c9dd8e943288a5eaebb180df), Lite checkout only rejects an already-linked subscription, then [creates a Checkout Session](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/38bb38ecb2b50f81c9dd8e943288a5eaebb180df/packages/console/core/src/billing.ts#L312-L348) using `customer_email` when the workspace has no linked customer. There is no idempotency key or pending reservation, so concurrent, retried, or stale Sessions can race, and `customer_email` can yield duplicate Stripe customers. This is a code-path/race finding; it does not assert that specific Checkout Sessions were observed in production.
- The first [`customer.subscription.created` webhook](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/38bb38ecb2b50f81c9dd8e943288a5eaebb180df/packages/console/app/src/routes/stripe/webhook.ts#L108-L159) claims the workspace; a later subscription under another customer throws `Customer ID mismatch`. Its [`invoice.payment_succeeded` lookup](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/38bb38ecb2b50f81c9dd8e943288a5eaebb180df/packages/console/app/src/routes/stripe/webhook.ts#L235-L242), keyed only by the linked customer, also throws. The later Stripe subscription can therefore stay paid while workspace linkage and entitlement fail.
- We need concurrency tests for Session creation/webhook ordering and reconciliation tests for paid subscriptions not linked to workspace billing.

Even though my main need is final state flushing rather than loop re-entry, it points to the same lifecycle gap: plugins need hooks around the point where OpenCode is about to stop using a session or run, instead of relying only on `session.idle` after the run has already become idle.

I support this. A concrete use case is memory plugins that need reliable lifecycle hooks to persist session state. `session.idle` works as a per-run signal, but it does not provide a clear finalization point for flushing pending state when OpenCode is done with a main session or a task-created subagent session.

Updated the issue body with new findings verified on origin/v2 at 175d200e53.

The key addition: losing the registration/boot race is not just a delayed activation, it is permanent. The supervisor's only reload triggers are the forked boot reload and config `Event.Updated`, `SdkPlugins.register` publishes nothing, and the Location cache never expires under active traffic. I reproduced this deterministically at two levels: a core test that polls for 2 seconds after post-boot registration (never appears, then activates immediately after one manually published config event), and an embedded SDK test where the already-booted Location never sees the plugin while a Location booted after registration does.

This means the fix needs both halves: gating Location readiness on initial activation (this issue) and making post-boot registration either apply or fail loudly (#34799).

Hard evidence for this from the anomalyco/opencode#35556 investigation, verified on origin/v2 at 175d200e53: a plugin registered through `opencode.plugin(...)` after a Location has booted never activates in that Location. A core-level test polls the plugin registry and materialized tools for 2 seconds after registration and sees nothing, then activates immediately after one config `Event.Updated`, which is the supervisor's only post-boot reload trigger. With `LocationServiceMap`'s 60 minute idle TTL never expiring under continuous traffic, a long-lived host waits forever unless a config file happens to change.

So the current documented behavior is not just an ordering invariant for hosts to enforce, it is a silent no-op with no error and no recovery path in a steady-state process. Whichever way the policy lands (apply to booted Locations or reject loudly), silent success should stop being an outcome.
